Two shares multiplied. First, 12.81% of diagnoses enter metastatic castration-sensitive disease each year. 6.8% of US cases are metastatic at diagnosis and de novo cases are 45% of the men living with metastatic prostate cancer (Devasia et al., Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev 2023;32(5):659-65, doi:10.1158/1055-9965.EPI-22-1038, PMC10159917; its base case gives de novo and recurrent disease the same survival, so the incidence split is the prevalence split): 0.068 / 0.45 = 15.11% of diagnoses become metastatic. Less the men whose first metastases are already castration-resistant: 1,019 of 5,096 US patients starting first-line mCRPC therapy (20.0%) came from non-metastatic CRPC (Flatiron; Hooper et al., JAMA Netw Open 2026;9(6):e2620750, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.20750), on the book's 11.5% mCRPC share: 0.1511 - 0.115 x 0.200 = 12.81%, about 40,200 men a year. Second, 17.86% carry a protocol-defined HRR alteration: 1,054 of 5,903 men with mCSPC prescreened for AMPLITUDE with a valid result (Attard et al., Nat Med 2025, doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03961-8). 0.1281 x 0.1786 = 0.02288, about 7,180 men a year
column12: the HRRm cohort only: AMPLITUDE, the one PARP add-on Phase 3 in this setting to report, was run in HRR-altered men, and EvoPAR-Prostate01's non-HRRm cohort would take the pool to all 40,200 if it reads out positive. Cross-check on the same basis: 79.3% of first-line mCRPC patients came from mHSPC (Hooper 2026), so 0.115 x 0.793 = 9.11% of diagnoses reach mCRPC from mHSPC, 71% of the 12.81% entering it, which leaves room for deaths before castration resistance. Devasia back-calculates from 2000 to 2017 SEER data and distant-stage incidence rose 5.3% a year in men 45 to 74 and 6.5% in men 75 and over to 2018 (Desai et al., JAMA Netw Open 2022, jamanetwork.com/journals/jamanetworkopen/fullarticle/2790041), so the pool leans low. The case for a smaller pool: AMPLITUDE enrolled every protocol-defined HRR alteration, 56% of them BRCA1 or BRCA2, yet FDA approved Akeega only 'for the treatment of patients with BRCA2-mutated metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer' (Johnson & Johnson press release, 2025-12-12), so a saruparib label narrower than the HRRm cohort is a live risk

column12: analogue, the most arguable figure here. The ratio does not depend on the Spanish positivity rate: Adelphi's own pooled figures, HRR alterations known in 13% of mCSPC and 18% of mCRPC patients, give (0.13 / 0.1786) x (0.07 / 0.18) = 0.283, and its 38% positivity among the men tested says testing is selective, which a ratio of the two settings absorbs. The case for more: HRR gene testing in metastatic prostate cancer rose 17 points, 26% to 43%, between the 2020 and 2022-2023 waves of the same programme and AMPLITUDE supports testing as routine in mCSPC; saruparib is PARP1-selective, where 25% of AMPLITUDE's niraparib arm needed a transfusion. The case for less: this gives saruparib the whole PARP class, and FDA approved Akeega (niraparib with abiraterone) in BRCA2-mutated mCSPC on 2025-12-12 (Johnson & Johnson press release), so saruparib would launch as the second PARP option in the setting; Akeega reached 93 Medicare Part D beneficiaries in 2025 (CMS file 4ff7c618); and in first-line mCRPC, where the PARP and ARPI combinations are labelled, PARP-based regimens stayed under 2.5% of starts across 2021 to 2025 (Hooper 2026)
